claim: Let \(k\) be an algebraically closed field of characteristic \(0\), and let \(\Gamma\) be a finite group. With \(\mu(\Gamma)=\min\{n\ge0:\Gamma\hookrightarrow S_n\}\) and \(S_0=\{1\}\), the minimum embedding dimension of a finite-dimensional monomial \(k\)-algebra \(A\) satisfying \(\pi_0\operatorname{Aut}_k(A)\cong\Gamma\) is exactly \(\mu(\Gamma)\); an explicit orbit-monomial ideal attains the bound and has \(\operatorname{Aut}_k(A)\cong\operatorname{Aut}_k(A)^0\rtimes\Gamma\) with solvable identity component.

assumptions: Algebraically closed field of characteristic zero
scientific_limitations_and_integrity.integrity: The claim is supported by a deductive proof and inspected primary literature; no independent audit or external certification is asserted.
limitations: Minimizes embedding dimension, not quotient vector-space dimension or number of monomial generators
For the trivial group, the minimum depends on whether the zero-variable algebra k is admitted

title: Exact minimal embedding dimension for prescribed component groups of monomial-algebra automorphisms
